claims.nodeLabel: CAP Registry / CAPCO Register of control systems, compartments and sub-compartments
claims.sourceText: CAPCO Register and Manual v5.1, Special Access Program Markings
claims.text: CAPCO Register v5.1: 'The first value in the SAP category is the SAP category indicator either "SPECIAL ACCESS REQUIRED-" or "SAR-" (the authorized abbreviation) ... Following the SAP category indicator shall be the SAP program indicator which is the program's nickname or authorized digraph or trigraph.'

claims.nodeLabel: CAP Registry / CAPCO Register of control systems, compartments and sub-compartments
claims.sourceText: CAPCO Register and Manual v5.1, change log
claims.text: CAPCO Register v5.1 change log records that the edition 'Moved the Special Access Required (SAR) marking from the Non-Intelligence Community Dissemination Control Markings category to a new category called Special Access Program Markings.'

claims.nodeLabel: CAP Registry / CAPCO Register of control systems, compartments and sub-compartments
claims.sourceText: CAPCO Register and Manual v5.1, title page
claims.text: CAPCO Register v5.1 title page: 'Certain security markings were removed due to classified content. These markings have been compiled in separate classified addenda.'

claims.nodeLabel: CAP Registry / CAPCO Register of control systems, compartments and sub-compartments
claims.sourceText: CAPCO Register and Manual v5.1, title page note
claims.text: The existence of classified addenda to the marking register means that a document could bear a compartment marking that is not listed in any public authority, so a researcher holding a released document cannot always determine from public sources what control system it belongs to. Reasoning: the register itself states that markings were removed for classification and compiled separately.
